title: Ideological asymmetry in the reach of pro-Russian digital disinformation to United States audiences
screen_reason: Hand-coded content analysis of a random 10,000-tweet English-language subsample of a 481,567-tweet MH17 keyword corpus gives the share of tweets that were pro-Russian disinformation (5.5%), a CONTENT estimate with a stated denominator. The paper's headline results are model-predicted conditional probabilities of potential exposure to disinformation by ideology and party registration, extracted as flagged REACH rows.

estimates.country: not restricted (English-language tweets from the global Twitter stream)
estimates.date: tweets from 10 July 2014 to the November 2016 collection date; 86% posted before 13 October 2015
estimates.measure_type: % of MH17-related English-language tweets hand-coded as pro-Russian disinformation
estimates.value_raw: Category 1: Pro-Russia, Proportion 5.5% (recoded Disinformation); Category 2: Pro-Ukraine 10.3%; Category 3: Other 84.1%
estimates.denominator: 10,000 English-language tweets randomly drawn from a 481,567-tweet MH17 keyword sample collected from the Twitter Gardenhose (10% random stream)
estimates.definition: tweet explicitly stated that Russia was not responsible for the MH17 crash, or that Ukraine was responsible, contrary to the Dutch Safety Board finding that a Buk missile was fired from separatist-held territory
estimates.misinfo_def: While misinformation is typically defined only in terms of incorrectness, disinformation is understood here as false information created for the strategic purpose of deceit
estimates.source_quote: 1: Pro-Russia 5.5% · Detailed analysis: MH17 shot down Disinformation (1)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Four coders each hand-coded a quarter of the 10,000-tweet subsample against a codebook (Supplementary Appendix A), with a shared 100-tweet subset for reliability: Cohen's kappa = .80, Krippendorff's alpha = .78. External ground truth was the Dutch Safety Board (2015) report and the 2018 Joint Investigation Team finding. Coding deliberately prioritised precision over recall.
estimates.moderator_quote: We collected the tweets from the Twitter Gardenhose, a 10% random sample of the full Twitter stream, ensuring a representative sample of tweets matching the search constraints. ... We identified disinformation by first drawing a random sample of 10,000 English-language tweets from the tweet sample. ... Based on these facts, we considered as a ground truth that pro-Russian separatists, with the help of Russia, were responsible for the downing of the MH17, and we considered attempts to argue otherwise as disinformation.
estimates.notes: Single-event keyword corpus (MH17), so topical denominator, not a general news diet. The authors state the figure is a lower bound: 'the coding strategy prioritized precision over recall and our estimated share of pro-Russian disinformation in the hand-coded subsample should be considered a lower-bound estimate.' The residual 84.1% Other category is mostly grief and headline tweets that took no position on responsibility, so 5.5% is a share of ALL MH17 tweets, not a share of tweets that made a responsibility claim (5.5/15.8 = 35% of position-taking tweets, not extracted because that ratio is not stated in the paper). Source quote replaced (it was a reconstruction of the whole table with ellipses) with the single contiguous Table 1 row that carries the value: category 1, Pro-Russia, 5.5%, recoded as Disinformation. The other two rows of the same table, quotable separately, are "2: Pro-Ukraine 10.3%" and "3: Other 84.1%", with the note that proportions sum to less than 100% due to rounding.

estimates.date: followers retrieved November 2016; voter-file matched user set from Barbera (2016)
estimates.measure_type: modelled conditional probability that a non-Republican-registered US Twitter user's potential exposure to MH17 information was disinformation
estimates.value_raw: For individuals not registered as Republican, the conditional probability of exposure to disinformation was 3.4%
estimates.denominator: predicted probability of potential exposure to any MH17 information, among 441,261 US Twitter accounts matched to public voter files (bivariate multinomial logit)
estimates.definition: potential exposure = the user follows at least one account that posted a tweet in the hand-coded subsample; disinformation = that tweet was coded pro-Russian (Category 1)
estimates.misinfo_def: disinformation is understood here as false information created for the strategic purpose of deceit
estimates.source_quote: For individuals not registered as Republican, the conditional probability of exposure to disinformation was 3.4%.
estimates.page_loc: Results, Followers' demographic characteristics (p. 184); Figure 3 bottom-left panel
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same four-coder hand-coding of the 10,000-tweet subsample (kappa = .80, alpha = .78) against the Dutch Safety Board report; party registration taken from public voter files matched by name, home state and geolocated county (Barbera 2016).
estimates.moderator_quote: In this analysis, we refer to followers of accounts spreading pro-Russian disinformation as having potential exposure to disinformation. While we cannot know whether actual users in the follower set saw the MH17 coverage contained in the tweet subsample, they were potentially exposed to it, insofar as the tweet would have appeared on their Twitter home timeline.
estimates.notes: JUDGEMENT CALL for the adjudicator. Three reasons to treat this row cautiously: (a) it is a model-predicted probability from a multinomial logit, not an observed count; (b) the denominator is not the population but the modelled probability of potential exposure to ANY MH17 information, so it is a share of a single event's information flow; (c) 'potential exposure' means following an account that tweeted, not seeing the tweet. Included because these party-registration figures are the paper's headline result and no unconditional prevalence is reported anywhere. The paper also notes this association shrinks sharply once age and sex are controlled. Quote trimmed to the sentence that carries this row's value and is contiguous in the text rendering; the following sentence (the Republican-registered 69.7%) is split by a line-break hyphen in "condi-tional".

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The abstract's headline pair, 6.5% (most liberal) to 45.2% (most conservative), is the SAME conditional-probability quantity computed on the 12.4M-user estimated-ideology set instead of the voter-file set. Not extracted as separate rows to avoid duplicating one modelled quantity four times; the party-registration pair was preferred because the authors themselves introduce the voter-file set to rule out bots contaminating the ideology set ('it may contain automated accounts built to mimic real users'). An adjudicator who prefers the ideology version should swap rows 2-3 for 6.5% / 45.2%, denominator 12,361,427 users. (2) 'Pro-Ukraine 10.3%' and 'Other 84.1%' are the non-disinformation categories, not misinformation shares. (3) 25 liberal versus 52 conservative high-influence accounts is a bare count of accounts with no share of exposure or sharing, so it fails R1 and is unusable as CONCENTRATION. (4) '86% of the tweets in the tweet sample were posted prior to the publication of the final report' is a timing statistic, not a misinformation share. (5) No unconditional prevalence of exposure or reach is reported anywhere in the paper: Figure 2 and Figure 3 show that predicted probabilities of any exposure were 'low and relatively invariant' but no number is given in text.

rob.design: Case-based observational design on one event (MH17, July 2014). Tweet sample: 481,567 tweets matching five MH17 keywords/hashtags, drawn from the Twitter Gardenhose 10% random stream, 10 July 2014 to November 2016; a random 10,000 English-language tweets were hand-coded by four coders (one quarter each) into pro-Russia / pro-Ukraine / other, with a shared 100-tweet subset giving Cohen's kappa = .80 and Krippendorff's alpha = .78; the coding scheme was deliberately narrow, prioritising precision over recall, and the authors call the disinformation share a lower bound. Audience data: all followers of the 7,230 non-protected accounts among the 8,575 accounts in the subsample (12,552,843 unique followers, retrieved November 2016 rather than at tweet time), matched to Barbera's 12.4M estimated-ideology set (collected 2012-2014, restricted to users following five or more political accounts) and to a 441,000-account voter-file-matched set. Exposure is 'potential' (following an account), not observed viewing; overlaps between sets are small (1.6M, 29k, 17k) and non-random, which the authors handle by modelling non-overlap as a third outcome. No classifier was used because standard classifiers had insufficient precision and recall.
rob.item6_quote: Pro-Russia tweets (Category 1) explicitly stated that Russia was not responsible for the MH17 crash (or that Ukraine was responsible).
rob.item10_quote: We identified disinformation by first drawing a random sample of 10,000 English-language tweets from the tweet sample. In the following, we refer to this as the tweet subsample. ... Table 1 presents the categories used in the manual coding, the proportions of tweets assigned to each category, and examples of tweets from each category.
